# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for reporting, coordinating, and reviewing operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures a consistent and effective response to incidents that may affect the safety, security, or efficiency of airport operations. The policy applies to all incidents that occur on airside, landside, or within airport facilities, including those involving equipment, personnel, and security. The scope includes but is not limited to incidents related to baggage handling, restricted items, ramp safety, and equipment malfunctions. All staff members are required to be familiar with and adhere to the procedures outlined in this policy to ensure a timely and coordinated response.

Operational incidents may range from minor disruptions to serious safety or security breaches that require immediate attention. The procedures outlined in this policy are designed to minimize the impact of such incidents, ensure the safety of personnel and passengers, and support a thorough review process to prevent recurrence. The effectiveness of the response is critical to maintaining the operational integrity of the airport and ensuring compliance with regulatory and internal standards. This policy is a key component of the airport's broader risk management and incident management framework.

## 2. Incident Categories

Operational incidents are categorized into four main types: baggage incidents, restricted-item incidents, ramp safety incidents, and equipment incidents. Each category has specific characteristics and potential impacts on airport operations. Baggage incidents may involve lost, delayed, or damaged luggage, or issues related to baggage handling equipment. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery of prohibited items, such as weapons or explosives, within airport premises. Ramp safety incidents include any event that poses a risk to personnel or aircraft on the ramp, such as unsecured vehicles or equipment. Equipment incidents refer to malfunctions or failures of critical airport equipment, including baggage systems, ground support equipment, or communication systems.

Each incident category may require a different level of response and coordination. For example, restricted-item incidents may involve immediate security escalation and coordination with law enforcement, while baggage incidents may require coordination with baggage handling teams and customer service. The categorization ensures that incidents are addressed according to their severity and potential impact. All incidents must be reported promptly and accurately to ensure a timely and effective response. The categorization also facilitates the tracking and review of incidents to identify trends and implement preventive measures.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All operational incidents must be reported immediately by the staff member who discovers or is involved in the incident. The reporting staff member is responsible for providing a clear and concise description of the incident, including the location, time, and any immediate actions taken. The report should be made to the appropriate supervisor or through the designated reporting mechanism, such as the airport's incident reporting system. The first response should focus on ensuring the safety of personnel and passengers, mitigating any immediate risks, and preserving evidence if required.

Once an incident is reported, the airside duty manager is responsible for initiating the initial response and coordinating with relevant teams. The airside duty manager must ensure that all necessary resources are available to address the incident and that any affected areas are secured. The incident coordinator is then assigned to oversee the response and ensure that all procedures are followed. The reporting staff member must remain at the scene until the incident is fully resolved or until relieved by a designated person. Prompt and accurate reporting is essential to maintaining the safety and efficiency of airport operations.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. The incident record must include all relevant details, such as the nature of the incident, the location, time, and any actions taken. The Incident Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all necessary information is captured and that the incident is logged in the airport's incident management system. The Incident Coordinator must also coordinate with the relevant teams and departments to ensure a coordinated and effective response.

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for maintaining communication with all involved parties, including the airside duty manager, security personnel, and affected operational teams. The Incident Coordinator must ensure that all incident-related information is accurately documented and that any required follow-up actions are initiated. The Incident Coordinator must also monitor the progress of the incident response and ensure that any escalations are handled in accordance with the relevant policies. The Incident Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring that the airport's response to operational incidents is both timely and effective.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an incident, a post-incident review meeting must be conducted to assess the incident and determine the root cause. The review meeting is led by the Incident Coordinator and includes representatives from the relevant departments and teams involved in the incident. The meeting must be held within a reasonable timeframe, as defined in section 5 of this policy, to ensure that all relevant information is still available and that lessons learned can be effectively applied. The review must include a detailed analysis of the incident, including the sequence of events, the actions taken, and any contributing factors.

The review meeting must document the cause of the incident and the corrective actions required to prevent recurrence. All participants must contribute to the discussion and provide any additional information that may be relevant. The findings of the review must be recorded in the incident record and shared with all relevant stakeholders. The corrective actions identified during the review must be implemented promptly and monitored to ensure effectiveness. The post-incident review is a critical component of the airport's continuous improvement process and helps to enhance the safety and efficiency of operations.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in the airport's incident management system and retained for the required period as defined by applicable regulations and internal policies. Each incident record must include a detailed description of the incident, the date and time of occurrence, the location, the individuals involved, and the actions taken. The record must also include the results of the post-incident review and any corrective actions implemented. All records must be accessible to authorized personnel and must be reviewed periodically to ensure their accuracy and completeness. The records serve as a valuable resource for training, analysis, and compliance purposes.
